original_observation_scope: Across five previously published tasks/datasets (one attention, four Stroop/Flanker control) paper compares model-simulation predicted learning/transfer to published participant behavior; not five new independently recruited participant cohorts and not brain activity recording.

source failures under nonlinear feature rewards/contexts and generalization restrictions

source_adverse_original.negative: Linear/additive feature approximation is structural assumption and can fail in nonlinear control–context interactions, yielding source maladaptive overexertion in particular reward scenarios.

source_adverse_original.source: original five prior empirical datasets and simulated comparison
source_adverse_original.negative: Successful fit to earlier published behavior does not constitute new original human experiments nor direct implementation proof; numerical posterior and human behavior distinct.
RW and WSLS model alternatives can capture portions of learning, LVOC relative improvement is bounded by task and original fitted variant set, not universal strategy selector proof.
Proposed dopaminergic dACC neural learning is expressly SPECULATION, and SARSA approximate rule is NOT the same algorithm as Gaussian Bayes posterior used in simulations.

No direct evidence the mind performs exact posterior sampling, reward priors/cost weights supplied or model-fixed, reward-rate/latency scales task-specific; nonstationarity/generalized planning untested.
Old uncorrected proof is not final canonical scientific version; any source equation change across proofs requires canonical official original PDF only.
